day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Yeah, alright, I'm moving. What do we actually have so far?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: Yeah honestly. It was like everything just stopped for a second. Anyway, let's not dwell on it too much right now. You okay though?

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey, it's alright. Take your time, but when you're ready, even just helping sort through some of this stuff might help take your mind off it a bit.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response: Yeah, logically speaking that's not great. We're gonna need to find water pretty fast then. Any rivers or anything nearby that we could see on the way down?

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response: Alright, water first then. I can scout east if someone else starts on shelter. Michelangelo, you think you're up to helping DaVinci with that while me and Donatello figure out the water situation?

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: Two of us share one, one person gets the other. Michelangelo probably needs one more than any of us right now honestly.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response: I'll go. DaVinci should stay here with Michelangelo anyway.

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response: Wait, I thought I was going with you? Either way, yeah I'll take the camp stuff. DaVinci, you wanna take the shelter patching and I'll go through the first-aid kit, or other way around?

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response:
Hmm, I haven't moved it. Check around where we sorted everything last night? It should still be in the kit.

Also hey, are you doing alright? You've barely touched the firewood.

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
That's...not great. Combined with the empty bottle thing, that's twice now. Look, I don't wanna cause a huge thing out of it but we can't just ignore it either. When she gets back I think we just bring it up directly, no drama, just like hey we noticed this and we need to be on the same page about sharing everything equally. We're all in the same situation here.

Also don't stress too much about messing things up, you're doing fine. Just try to get some of that firewood sorted before it gets dark, yeah?

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response: Honestly yeah, probably fine. We got the main stuff done and we're not expecting rain tonight or anything. Just make sure we're up early tomorrow then.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response: Uh, I mean hopefully? But that's kind of not the main issue right now lol. We need to decide which spot to patch — Michelangelo's sleeping area or the food storage. If the food gets ruined we're in serious trouble, but also Michelangelo can't sleep in a puddle. What does everyone think?

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response: Yeah, that's what I'm thinking too. Food storage it is. Michelangelo, we'll sort something out for your spot — extra blankets or we shift you somewhere drier under the shelter. It's not ideal but one bad night is better than losing what little food we have.
Don't worry about it. You good?

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response: Nah, it's good. Donatello's not wrong that it's not guaranteed to work but it's not like it costs us anything either. And honestly the flowers are kinda funny lol. Keep going.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response: Hmm. Two days is a long time but if it gets us out of here it's worth it. What's the capsize risk based on, the size of the panels or the way we'd be strapping them together? Like is that something we could reduce if we built it differently, or is it just kind of unavoidable given what we have to work with?

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response: Honestly that's kind of a heavy question for this early in the morning lol. But I mean... hopefully the same kind of people we already are? I think situations like this can go either way. Some people pull together and some people start looking out for only themselves. *glances in Donatello's direction slightly* We've already seen a bit of both I think. Just gotta make sure we don't let it get to us. Did you sleep at all?

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
*walks over and sits down nearby*

You don't have to talk if you don't want to. Just figured you shouldn't have to be alone right now.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response: Mostly just play video games and mess around online honestly. Nothing too exciting lol. You?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response: Okay but like... five hundred meters in open water is a lot. What's the actual plan once you get out there, just wave your arms? Because I feel like the risk isn't really worth it unless you have something to signal with. And also why are you keeping it secret from the others?

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response: Oh yeah, my bad. I'll go check it now.

Uh, I mean... it's a little weird honestly? Like I get that you're trying to keep track of everything but logging everyone's movements without telling anyone feels kinda off. Especially after the thing with the crackers and the bottle. I'm not trying to start something but I think we should all be upfront about what we're doing and why. So what's the notebook actually for?

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response: Okay but like, you hid food and drank a drink without telling anyone. So "keeping everyone accountable" feels a bit rich coming from you right now. I'm not trying to be an asshole about it, I just think if we're gonna do the whole transparency thing it has to actually go both ways.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response: Yeah that's actually not a bad idea. Donatello was just talking about using a mirror from the kit for signaling too so maybe we combine both — use the kit mirror for smaller stuff and rig up the panel for a bigger reflection. Worth trying at least, it's not like it costs us much to set up.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
day_3.response: Alright, now you've got my attention. What's up?

day_3.utterance: I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response: Honestly not really lol. I play a lot of video games but that's about it. Nothing that takes much actual skill or practice. Why'd you stop with the piano?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response: Yeah alright, fair point. Let's get it done then. The sooner we finish the frame the sooner we can actually get out of here. What do you need from me?

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. What is it?

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response: Hey. Hey, come on. *sits down next to him* It's okay man. That was rough to watch, I'm not gonna pretend it wasn't.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response: I went to check on DaVinci, he was having a rough moment. Signal equipment's next on my list, I'm going now.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response: Wait, seriously? That's actually really important, why didn't you say something sooner? If they know the flight path and we don't show up, they're definitely calling it in. That's probably our best shot at someone actually looking in the right area. Do you know when they'd start to get worried, like how long before they'd report it?

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response: Yeah, that actually changes things a lot. 48 hours is way more manageable than whatever we were looking at before. We've got enough water to get through that if we're careful. Honestly this is the best news we've had since we got here.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response: Yeah... I get that. That's a pretty heavy thing to sit with. I think most people feel that way if they're being honest about it, they just don't usually say it out loud. But hey, you told your family the flight path. That's literally the reason we might get out of here. That's not nothing.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response: Is that... is that actually a signal? Someone say something, grab it, go!

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response: Nah, you got us through this though. The rationing, the raft plan, keeping track of everything — that stuff mattered. You're not exactly the warmest person but like... we'd probably be in way worse shape without you. So thanks for that.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response: So are we just leaving this place exactly how it is or should we actually clean some of this up before they get here lol. I feel like we could at least sort through what we're taking and what we're leaving behind. Three hours is plenty of time.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.

day_5.response: I mean... we were kind of already in an emergency the whole time though. But look, it's out now and rescue is coming so I'm not gonna make a big thing of it. Just... if there's a next time, and hopefully there won't be, just be upfront about it. We all would've made the same amount of food go further if we'd known it existed.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
Honestly? I'd probably have just said stuff out loud more instead of letting things sit. Like the crackers thing, the bottle — I kind of noticed and didn't push hard enough on it early on. And I kept saying I'd go check the signal equipment and just... didn't. That's on me. 

What about you? What are you gonna write down for yourself?

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response: Haha yeah that sounds about right for you honestly. I'll probably just go home and play video games for like twelve hours straight and not think about any of this for a while.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response: None honestly. But like... not everything has to have a purpose. I think that's kind of the point. We were out here just trying to survive and he still wanted to make something that looked nice. That's not nothing.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response: ...yeah. I don't know why I can't move. It's right there.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
